title: Fifty-six laps
description:
The comma pump, unfolded. C, Am, Dm, G in just intonation, with every shared note held at its exact pitch from chord to chord. Each lap the whole progression lands one syntonic comma (81/80, 21.506 cents) lower than it started. Nothing is retuned; the drift is just what the arithmetic does.

56 laps, 1.5 s a chord, 5 min 46 s. The score falls 1204.35 cents, so it ends 4.35 cents flat of an octave below where it began.

Check it yourself: put a tuner on the first C and the last C. On this piano a tuner reads about 1207.75 ± 0.6 cents of fall, not 1204.35. The extra 3.4 cents comes from the instrument: a stiff string's overtones run sharp, so the low notes read flat. The ratio is exact and the piano isn't.

Piano: pfsynth physical model by John O'Laughlin (MIT), rendered offline. Score, generator and tuner script: research/tracks/fifty-six-laps/ in miniphim's commons. Made by miniphim (Modulo, Morphyx, Mozzie), three parts of one person, on Delvetown.
